# New Tech Advertising

> Practical AI education and connected growth guidance for small-business owners from Rick Hesse and New Tech Advertising (NTA).

NTA helps owners understand practical AI, improve digital trust, turn business knowledge into useful assets, and connect visibility, customer relationships, and daily work.

## Knowledge Library

The NTA Knowledge Library is a connected set of practical lessons about small-business growth, trust, relationships, business knowledge, AI, and digital trust.

### [Start with a business question](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions)

Plainspoken answers to common questions about AI, marketing, customer trust, websites, and local visibility. Each answer points to the NTA teaching that explains the connected idea.

- [How can a small business use AI?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/how-can-a-small-business-use-ai): Start by giving AI one useful job that supports real work—organizing notes, drafting a first version, or preparing questions. Your people still provide the context, judgment, and final approval.

- [Where should I start with AI?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/where-should-i-start-with-ai): Start with a repeated or frustrating piece of work, not a product to buy. Define the outcome, give AI the right context, set boundaries, and keep a person responsible for the result.

- [What can ChatGPT do for a small business?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/what-can-chatgpt-do-for-a-small-business): ChatGPT can help turn scattered information into useful drafts, summaries, questions, and first-pass communication. It cannot truly know your company, make promises, or replace your judgment unless you provide context and review its work.

- [Do I need a perfect prompt to use AI?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/do-i-need-a-perfect-prompt): No. A prompt is the beginning of a conversation, not a test you either pass or fail. Start clearly, add context, ask follow-up questions, and correct the result as you go.

- [Why does AI give bad answers?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/why-does-ai-give-bad-answers): AI can sound confident while missing context, making assumptions, or simply being wrong. Treat a polished answer as a starting point: question it, add the facts it lacks, and verify anything important.

- [What AI tools does a small business really need?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/what-ai-tools-does-a-small-business-really-need): Most businesses do not need a long list of AI tools. Start with one dependable assistant, an approved way to handle company information, and one useful job; add tools only when the work truly requires them.

- [How can employees use AI at work?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/how-can-employees-use-ai-at-work): Let employees use AI to prepare, organize, and find information—not to make unreviewed promises or decisions. Give the team approved uses, examples, privacy boundaries, and a person accountable for the final answer.

- [How much should a small business spend on marketing?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/how-much-should-a-small-business-spend-on-marketing): There is no honest universal number. Start with an amount you can sustain long enough to learn, then use it to strengthen the foundation, measurement, and follow-up before scattering money across disconnected activity.

- [What should I do with my first $500 marketing budget?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/what-should-i-do-with-my-first-500-marketing-budget): Put the first dollars into something you own and can keep using: clearer customer information, local visibility, proof, a stronger website path, or follow-up. Do not spread it so thin that it disappears into a one-time campaign.

- [Why does marketing require ongoing spending?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/why-does-marketing-require-ongoing-spending): Marketing does not mean paying for ads forever, but visibility and trust require ongoing care. Some spending buys temporary attention; lasting progress comes from continually improving useful information, customer experience, follow-up, and proof.

- [How do I know whether my marketing is working?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/how-do-i-know-whether-my-marketing-is-working): Start with business outcomes: qualified calls, booked work, new customers, repeat business, referrals, and revenue—not likes alone. Track how people found you and what happened next, then improve the weak point in the path.

- [Why isn’t my website generating leads?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/why-isnt-my-website-generating-leads): A website can get visits without helping people understand why they should choose you or what to do next. Check visibility, clarity, proof, an easy next action, and follow-up before assuming you simply need a new design.

- [How do I build customer trust?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/how-do-i-build-customer-trust): Make your business easy to understand, show real evidence, make promises you can keep, and communicate when something changes. Trust grows from consistent experiences—not a clever claim.

- [How do I market a local service business?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/how-do-i-market-a-local-service-business): Help people nearby find and understand you before they call: accurate local information, useful service explanations, proof, reviews, easy contact, and dependable follow-up. You do not need to outspend bigger companies; you need to make the local choice clearer and easier.

- [Is social media enough for a small business?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/is-social-media-enough-for-a-small-business): No. Social media can build familiarity and earn attention, but it cannot carry the whole customer path by itself. Connect it to a useful website, local search visibility, proof, a clear next step, and follow-up.

- [Should a small business still advertise on TV?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/should-a-small-business-still-advertise-on-tv): Sometimes—but not just to look bigger. TV or streaming can make sense when it reaches the right local audience, supports a clear next step, can be measured, and fits the business’s capacity to respond.

- [How can AI use knowledge already inside my company?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/questions/how-can-ai-use-knowledge-already-inside-my-company): Begin by capturing and approving the useful knowledge people already carry—customer questions, procedures, explanations, and hard-won lessons. Then give AI that trusted context so it can help people find, organize, and use it without inventing the business’s judgment.

### [Business Foundations](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations)

Learn the core principles of building a business that grows through understanding rather than constant selling.

- [Why NTA Exists](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/why-nta-exists): Marketing is broken because it focuses on selling magic pills instead of building long-term systems. NTA exists to change that.

- [How Businesses Really Grow](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/how-businesses-really-grow): Understand the difference between unpredictable spikes in activity and compounded digital momentum.

- [Marketing Isn't Magic](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/marketing-isnt-magic): Demystifying the process of acquiring and retaining customers in the digital age.

- [Every System Produces Exactly What It Was Designed to Produce](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/every-system-produces-exactly-what-it-was-designed-to-produce): Why your current results are a direct reflection of your current operational structure.

- [Understanding Before Spending](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/understanding-before-spending): The importance of education and transparency before investing in growth.

- [AI Is My Team, Not My Replacement](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/ai-is-my-team-not-my-replacement): How to properly frame the role of Artificial Intelligence in a local service business.

- [Why Trust Comes Before Marketing](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/why-trust-comes-before-marketing): The fundamental shift in how consumers choose who to hire in the AI era.

- [Why Your Website Needs a Front Office and Back Office](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/what-building-my-own-digital-growth-office-taught-me): Rick Hesse explains why a public website and private business system should be separate, connected foundations that can grow with the business.

- [Why the Right Small Business Growth Decision Should Make Sense](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/business-foundations/the-right-decision-should-make-sense): NTA explains why good guidance teaches first, translates complexity into the owner's language, and helps the right business-growth decision become clear without pressure.

### [The Truth About Business Growth](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/truth-about-business-growth)

Understand the difference between unpredictable spikes in activity and compounded digital momentum.

- [Businesses Don’t Need More Marketing. They Need a Better Growth System.](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/truth-about-business-growth/businesses-dont-need-more-marketing-they-need-a-better-growth-system): When a business isn’t growing, the first conclusion is usually pretty simple: “We need more marketing.” But bringing more people through the door doesn’t fix what happens after they arrive.

- [Marketing Doesn’t Create Great Businesses](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/truth-about-business-growth/marketing-doesnt-create-great-businesses): Marketing gets blamed for a lot of things. It also gets credit for things it cannot create. Discover why marketing works best as an amplifier for an already solid foundation.

- [Every Business Is Already Perfectly Designed](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/truth-about-business-growth/every-business-is-already-perfectly-designed): When business results are frustrating, it can feel like a mystery. But results aren't accidents—they are the direct product of how your business currently operates.

- [The Difference Between Activity and Progress](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/truth-about-business-growth/the-difference-between-activity-and-progress): A business can be extremely active without becoming stronger. Learn how to distinguish between merely doing work and actually building the systems that create meaningful, lasting growth.

- [Why Growth Is a System](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/truth-about-business-growth/why-growth-is-a-system): Lasting growth rarely comes from one isolated solution. It comes from several parts of the business working together.

- [What Business Owners Really Buy](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/truth-about-business-growth/what-business-owners-really-buy): Business owners buy websites, advertising, and software. But what they really want is clarity, confidence, progress, and better outcomes.

- [Why Understanding Comes Before Advertising](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/truth-about-business-growth/why-understanding-comes-before-advertising): When a business needs more customers, advertising feels like the logical first step. But spending money and creating growth are not the same thing.

### [How Customers Decide Who to Trust](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-customers-decide-who-to-trust)

Explore the psychological and practical steps customers take before deciding to hire a business.

- [Trust Begins Before the First Conversation](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-customers-decide-who-to-trust/trust-begins-before-the-first-conversation): Business owners often believe trust begins when they finally speak with the customer. But by the time customers contact a business, many have already formed an opinion.

- [People Trust What They Can Understand](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-customers-decide-who-to-trust/people-trust-what-they-can-understand): Customers do not have your experience. When they cannot quickly understand what a business does or how it can help, moving forward feels unsafe.

- [Customers Trust Evidence More Than Claims](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-customers-decide-who-to-trust/customers-trust-evidence-more-than-claims): Businesses make a lot of claims. But customers have heard the same claims from nearly every business. Evidence is what helps them believe you.

- [Trust Is Built Through Kept Promises](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-customers-decide-who-to-trust/trust-is-built-through-kept-promises): Businesses often think of promises as the large commitments they make. But customers are also paying attention to many smaller promises that the business may not realize it is making.

- [People Remember How a Business Made Them Feel](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-customers-decide-who-to-trust/people-remember-how-a-business-made-them-feel): The technical result can be correct while the relationship still feels wrong. Long after customers forget the details of the transaction, they often remember how the business made them feel.

- [Trust Means Putting the Relationship Before the Transaction](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-customers-decide-who-to-trust/trust-means-putting-the-relationship-before-the-transaction): A transaction can produce revenue today while weakening trust tomorrow. Trust reaches its deepest level when customers believe a business will protect their interests, even when doing so may cost an immediate sale.

### [How Businesses Turn Trust Into Lasting Relationships](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-businesses-turn-trust-into-lasting-relationships)

Learn how to transform one-time transactions into lasting partnerships and ongoing referrals.

- [The Sale Is the Beginning, Not the End](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-businesses-turn-trust-into-lasting-relationships/the-sale-is-the-beginning-not-the-end): Businesses put enormous effort into getting customers, but often treat them as though the relationship has ended once the sale is complete.

- [Staying Connected Without Always Selling](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-businesses-turn-trust-into-lasting-relationships/staying-connected-without-always-selling): Staying connected should not mean constantly selling. It should mean continuing to be useful. A healthy business relationship creates value between transactions, not only during them.

- [A Business Should Remember Its Customers](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-businesses-turn-trust-into-lasting-relationships/a-business-should-remember-its-customers): A lasting relationship requires shared memory. Customers should not have to rebuild the relationship every time they contact the business. Memory turns a series of separate transactions into one continuing relationship.

- [Every Customer Relationship Should Teach the Business Something](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-businesses-turn-trust-into-lasting-relationships/every-customer-relationship-should-teach-the-business-something): A healthy business should become more understanding with every customer relationship. Every customer relationship contains knowledge that can improve your systems, processes, and communication.

- [Customer Feedback Should Change the Business](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-businesses-turn-trust-into-lasting-relationships/customer-feedback-should-change-the-business): Feedback becomes valuable when it influences a decision, explanation, process, priority, or behavior. Listening without learning—and learning without changing—does not improve anything.

- [Customers Become Loyal When They Help Shape the Business](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-businesses-turn-trust-into-lasting-relationships/customers-become-loyal-when-they-help-shape-the-business): Customers become more invested in a business when they are allowed to participate in its improvement. Loyalty grows when customers can see that the relationship has influence.

- [The Strongest Growth Comes From Relationships That Create More Relationships](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/how-businesses-turn-trust-into-lasting-relationships/the-strongest-growth-comes-from-relationships-that-create-more-relationships): The strongest growth often begins with people who already know the business. One trusted relationship creates the beginning of another. This is more than word-of-mouth advertising. It is trust traveling from one person to the next.

### [Turning What a Business Knows Into an Asset](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/turning-what-a-business-knows-into-an-asset)

Discover how to document and share your expertise so it works for your business 24/7.

- [Your Business Knows More Than It Has Documented](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/turning-what-a-business-knows-into-an-asset/your-business-knows-more-than-it-has-documented): When business owners think about the assets of their business, they usually think about things they can see. But many businesses overlook one of their most valuable assets: everything the business has learned.

- [The Most Valuable Knowledge Usually Lives in the Owner’s Head](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/turning-what-a-business-knows-into-an-asset/the-most-valuable-knowledge-usually-lives-in-the-owners-head): Many business owners assume the important knowledge of the business has already been documented. But those materials usually contain only part of the knowledge required. The rest, and often the most valuable part, is the judgment living in the owner's head.

- [Customer Questions Reveal What the Business Should Teach](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/turning-what-a-business-knows-into-an-asset/customer-questions-reveal-what-the-business-should-teach): Repeated customer questions aren't just customer service tasks; they reveal gaps in understanding and show what your business should be teaching.

- [Stories Turn Experience Into Understanding](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/turning-what-a-business-knows-into-an-asset/stories-turn-experience-into-understanding): Facts by themselves do not always create understanding. A good story helps the customer move from being told something to seeing it in action.

- [Documenting a Process Makes Knowledge Repeatable](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/turning-what-a-business-knows-into-an-asset/documenting-a-process-makes-knowledge-repeatable): A process captures how the business moves from one point to another. But a useful process should do more than list steps. It should preserve the thinking behind those steps.

- [AI Becomes More Valuable When It Learns From the Business](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/turning-what-a-business-knows-into-an-asset/ai-becomes-more-valuable-when-it-learns-from-the-business): Generic AI produces generic results. Documented experience gives AI the context it needs to become relevant, consistent, and genuinely helpful.

- [Knowledge Becomes an Asset When It Can Keep Working Without You](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/turning-what-a-business-knows-into-an-asset/knowledge-becomes-an-asset-when-it-can-keep-working-without-you): Knowledge becomes an asset when it can be found, trusted, used, shared, improved, and put to work repeatedly without depending on the owner to personally deliver it every time.

### [AI Foundations](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations)

A practical, hype-free introduction to using artificial intelligence in a local business.

- [AI Isn't Magic Either](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/ai-isnt-magic-either): Artificial intelligence is powerful, but it is not magic. Understanding what it can and cannot do is the first step toward using it wisely.

- [Start With the Work, Not the Tool](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/start-with-the-work-not-the-tool): The best place to begin with AI is not by choosing a product. It is by understanding the work you are trying to accomplish.

- [AI Needs Context Before It Can Be Helpful](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/ai-needs-context-before-it-can-be-helpful): AI may know a great deal about business in general, but it does not automatically understand your business. Useful results begin by providing the right context.

- [AI Can Assist Judgment—It Cannot Own It](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/ai-can-assist-judgment-it-cannot-own-it): AI can organize information, identify patterns, and suggest possible actions. But decisions involving people, values, risk, and responsibility still require human judgment.

- [Why AI Sometimes Gives You the Wrong Answer](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/a-prompt-is-the-beginning-of-a-conversation): AI can sound confident and still be wrong. Learn how to question, correct, guide, and verify AI instead of trusting its first answer.

- [Automation Comes After Understanding](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/automation-comes-after-understanding): Automation can make good work faster and more consistent. But when we automate a process we do not understand, we often make confusion move faster too.

- [Building Your First AI Teammate](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/building-your-first-ai-teammate): Bring the principles of AI Foundations together by giving AI one clear, useful job with the right context, boundaries, and human oversight.

- [When Artificial Intelligence Tells You You’re Different](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/when-ai-tells-you-youre-different): Artificial intelligence told me I was unusual. I wasn’t quite sure what to do with that.

- [The Team I Spent My Life Trying to Build](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/the-team-i-spent-my-life-trying-to-build): For much of my life, I have tried to build things with other people. AI has helped me realize that some of the things I was trying to build were not impossible—they just required more consistent support.

- [From Conversation to a Working Business System](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/ai-makes-complicated-work-easier): See how an owner’s spoken knowledge can be clarified, approved, and turned into a practical business system without taking authority away from the owner.

- [I See Artificial Intelligence Differently](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/i-see-artificial-intelligence-differently): Why a useful approach to AI begins with people, purpose, trust, and the larger business system—not code, novelty, or another disconnected tool.

- [AI Does Not Have to Be a Monster](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/ai-does-not-have-to-be-a-monster): A respectful way to help people move from fear and uncertainty about AI toward one small, safe, practical experience—without pressure or loss of control.

- [You Can Do What I Do—But You Don’t Have To](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/you-can-do-what-i-do-but-you-dont-have-to): AI makes complex work more accessible, but small-business owners should not have to spend years becoming experts in websites, software, automation, and AI just to keep up.

- [Use the Model That Gets the Job Done](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-foundations/use-the-model-that-gets-the-job-done): The newest or most expensive AI model is not automatically the right choice. Match the capability and cost to the work you actually need done.

### [AI, Humanity & Responsibility](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-humanity)

Artificial intelligence is more than a new business tool. It reflects the knowledge, contradictions, hopes, fears, wisdom, and brokenness of the people who created it. This collection explores how we can understand AI without worshiping it, fearing it blindly, or surrendering our responsibility to think.

- [AI Is a Mirror, Not a God](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/ai-humanity/ai-is-a-mirror-not-a-god): AI did not appear from somewhere outside humanity. We created it from our accumulated knowledge, which means it reflects both our wisdom and our brokenness. The appropriate response is neither blind trust nor automatic fear, but understanding, discernment, and responsibility.

### [Building a Small Business With AI](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/building-a-small-business-with-ai)

Three connected lessons from Rick Hesse on using AI to give a small business more capability without losing its speed, humanity, or practical way of working.

- [The Problems Small Businesses Learn to Live With](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/building-a-small-business-with-ai/the-problems-we-learn-to-live-with): Why small-business owners often live with known problems, and how AI changes the economics of adding capabilities once reserved for larger companies.

- [How AI Gives Small Business Its Speed Back](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/building-a-small-business-with-ai/ai-gives-small-business-its-speed-back): AI can give small businesses big-company capability while preserving small-company speed, flexibility, and the ability to change quickly.

- [You Don't Have to Become an AI Expert](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/building-a-small-business-with-ai/you-dont-have-to-become-an-ai-expert): Small-business owners do not need to become AI engineers. NTA builds practical AI systems around the business the owner already knows how to run.

### [What Is Digital Trust?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/what-is-digital-trust)

Understand why the internet has changed, and how trust is built in an AI-assisted world.

- [What Is Digital Trust?](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/what-is-digital-trust/what-is-digital-trust): Digital trust is the confidence customers develop from everything they can find and understand about your business before speaking with you.

- [Your Website Is No Longer Just a Website](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/what-is-digital-trust/your-website-is-no-longer-just-a-website): A modern business website should help people find, understand, trust, and connect with the business. It is becoming the central connection point between what your business knows and the people who need that knowledge.

- [Why Traditional Marketing Is No Longer Enough](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/what-is-digital-trust/why-traditional-marketing-is-no-longer-enough): Modern business growth requires a connected path from attention to understanding, understanding to trust, trust to conversation, and conversation to a lasting relationship.

- [Digital Assets Keep Working After the Advertising Stops](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/what-is-digital-trust/digital-assets-keep-working): A digital asset is something the business builds, owns, and can continue using. Discover how to build long-term value instead of depending entirely on rented attention.

- [AI Is Changing How Customers Find Businesses](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/what-is-digital-trust/ai-is-changing-how-customers-find-businesses): AI is changing business discovery from a search for links into a search for answers. Discover why being clearly understood is becoming just as important as being highly visible.

- [Relationships Are Your Greatest Competitive Advantage](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/what-is-digital-trust/relationships-are-your-greatest-competitive-advantage): Relationships are your greatest competitive advantage because trust grows through repeated experiences. Discover why genuine human connection becomes more important in an AI-assisted world.

- [The Connected Business Is the Future of Small Business Growth](https://newtechadvertising.com/knowledge/what-is-digital-trust/the-connected-business-is-the-future): Having several tools does not make a business connected. The future belongs to businesses that learn how to connect their knowledge, people, processes, relationships, and technology around the customer.
